intro: X (Twitter) fully supports Unicode symbols in posts, threads, replies, and bios. Use these characters to add structure to long threads, make hashtags stand out, decorate your bio, or add personality to individual posts. These are common, widely supported characters, but a very new or rare one can show as a box on an older device.

faq.q: What is the X (Twitter) symbol to copy and paste?
faq.a: People most often want the stylised X used for the rebranded Twitter logo. The closest copy-paste text characters are 𝕏 (mathematical double-struck capital X) and the cross marks ✕ ✗ ✘ ╳. X isn't an official font, so these Unicode characters are the standard way to represent the X mark in plain text.

faq.q: How do I add symbols to my X (Twitter) bio?
faq.a: Tap any symbol on this page to copy it, then paste it into your X bio, display name, or a post. X fully supports Unicode in bios, display names, posts, and replies: use dots, bars, and stars (· │ ✦ ⊹) to separate sections or add personality.

faq.q: Why do some symbols show as boxes on X?
faq.a: A blank box or question mark means the viewer's device doesn't have a glyph for that character. Well-supported characters (arrows, stars, checkmarks, basic punctuation) render everywhere; very new or rare symbols may not. If a symbol looks broken, pick a more common alternative.
